signals.title: test: fix double-stop penalty and grace period in logs agent tests
signals.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Sets `logs_config.stop_grace_period` to 0 and wraps `agent.stop()` in `sync.OnceFunc` in the logs agent test suites, reducing `TestRestartTestSuite` from 70s to 33s and `TestAgentTestSuite` from 41s to 17s. ### Motivation The cleanup registered by `createAgent` and the explicit `agent.stop()` calls in test methods both invoked `stopComponents`, which blocked for 5s each on non-idempotent component `Stop()` methods (e.g. `fileLauncher.Stop()` blocks on an unbuffered channel when `Start()` was never called); the 5s grace period added another 5s per call. ### Describe how you validated your changes Both test suites were run in full before and after the change to confirm all tests still pass and measure the speedup. ### Additional Notes All changes are test-only; no non-test code was modified.

signals.title: Report DDOT process state in the installer agent state
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds a `ddot_process_state` line to the agent state the fleet installer daemon reports through the remote-config client. It is set on the `datadog-agent` package entry, next to the existing stable/experiment version and config version. The state is read from `dd-procmgrd` over its socket (gRPC on a UDS on Linux, a named pipe on Windows — the `dd-procmgr` binary is never invoked) when the process manager supervises DDOT, and falls back to systemd on Linux / the service manager on Windows otherwise. This reuses `pkg/procmgr/coat`, which already performs exactly that collection for COAT telemetry and already carries a `ddot` entry in its service catalog; the new `Snapshot.ServiceProcessState` only maps a collected snapshot onto a reported value. Reported values: `running`, `starting`, `stopping`, `stopped`, `created`, `crashed`, `exited`, `failed` when procmgr supervises DDOT; `running` when the legacy systemd unit or Windows service is active; `not_installed` when DDOT is absent; `unknown` when procmgr owns it but is unreachable; and `""` only when nothing can be determined, so the backend can tell "not reported" from "no DDOT on this host". The probe is bounded (2s) and cannot fail a state refresh — it returns a string only, never an error. ### Motivation The update monitoring uses the reported agent state to decide whether an update succeeded. Now that DDOT can be updated on its own (version or config), the state had no way to express whether the DDOT process actually came back up afterwards. This matters because a broken DDOT does not end an experiment by itself: the core agent does not read `otel-config.yaml`, so the experiment agent stays healthy, and `dd-procmgrd` retries a failing child forever rather than giving up. The reported process state is therefore the only signal that can tell the backend not to promote. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit tests: - `pkg/procmgr/coat/process_state_test.go` — every `pb.ProcessState`, both legacy supervisor modes, not-installed, procmgr-unreachable, installed-without-supervisor, unknown service ID. - `pkg/fleet/daemon/ddot_state_test.go` — the collector seam (nil collector, procmgr running/failed, systemd, not-installed) and a `refreshState` test asserting the field lands only on the `datadog-agent` entry. - `pkg/fleet/daemon/local_api_test.go` — the field round-trips through the local API `/status`. Ran: `bazel test //pkg/procmgr/coat:coat_test //pkg/fleet/daemon:daemon_test`, `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/proto/pbgo/core` (msgp round-trip), `bazel build //cmd/installer/...`, `dda inv linter.go`. Generated protobuf code is committed and `dda inv protobuf.generate` is a no-op on the tree. E2E — new `TestDDOTConfigFailureReportsFailedAndReverts` in the fleet config suite (Linux, runs in the existing `new-e2e-fleet-config` job with no CI wiring changes): 1. Install the agent and the `ddot` extension; assert DDOT healthy under `dd-procmgrd`, launched with the stable `otel-config.yaml`, reported as `running`. 2. Start a config experiment patching `/otel-config.yaml` with an invalid debug-exporter verbosity; assert the broken config reaches the experiment collector and DDOT is unhealthy. 3. Assert the reported `ddot_process_state` becomes `failed`. 4. Assert nothing promoted it: `experiment_config_version` still set, `stable_config_version` unchanged, stable config free of the bad value. 5. Mimic the backend reacting to that state by sending the revert task (`stop_experiment_config`). 6. Assert the revert landed: `experiment_config_version` cleared, `stable_config_version` never changed, stable `otel-config.yaml` restored byte-for-byte, DDOT healthy under `dd-procmgrd` on the stable config, reported state back to `running`. ### Additional Notes - **The failure state is `failed`, not `crashed`.** `CRASHED` exists in the proto and Go enums but the Rust process manager never emits it: `set_last_status` maps any non-zero exit or signal to `Failed`. - **`restart: on-failure` never gives up on DDOT.** With `restart_sec: 2`, backoff ×2 capped at 60s, and `start_limit_burst: 5` over a 10s window, attempts land at t≈0, 2, 6, 14, 30, 62… — never 5 within any 10s window, so DDOT loops `Failed → Starting → Failed` indefinitely and `dd-procmgrd` stays up. - Field 17 is new, so older backends skip it and newer backends see `""` from older agents. The msgp decoder skips unknown fields, so mixed-version marshalling is safe. - During a version experiment, `Installed`/`ProcmgrConfigured` are resolved from the daemon's own install root while the process state comes from the shared procmgr socket. That only affects the `unknown`-vs-`stopped` distinction; the running state stays correct, since the stable and experiment procmgr share one socket and the DDOT process definition filename is invariant (only `${DD_CONF_DIR}` differs).

signals.title: [CWS] Decouple ring buffer read loop with a configurable dispatcher queue
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Decouples event processing from the eBPF ring buffer read loop in CWS. Events read from the kernel `BPF_MAP_TYPE_RINGBUF` are handed to a dedicated dispatcher goroutine via a user space queue instead of being processed inline on the read loop. Adds two settings under `event_monitoring_config.event_stream` (with the usual `runtime_security_config` deprecated aliases): - `dispatcher_queue_size` (integer, default `16384`) — size of the user space dispatcher queue. - `dispatcher_queue_size_per_core` (boolean, default `true`) — when set, `dispatcher_queue_size` is multiplied by the number of CPUs on the system. By default this yields a queue of `16384 * num_cores`. ### Motivation The kernel ring buffer can only be sized in powers of two of the page size, so it is a coarse and memory-expensive knob. When the (heavy) event handler runs inline on the read loop, a slow handler stalls draining of the kernel ring buffer and events are dropped under bursts. Moving processing onto a dispatcher goroutine lets the read loop keep draining into a roomier, fine-grained, configurable user space buffer, providing a cushion against event bursts. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `pkg/security/probe/eventstream/ringbuffer`, `pkg/security/probe/config`, and `pkg/security/probe` compile. - `dda inv schema.lint` passes; config bindings regenerated via `dda inv schema.codegen` / `dda inv schema.compress`. - TODO: functional/e2e coverage for the dispatcher and the new settings. ### Possible Drawbacks / Trade-offs - The queue is a burst cushion, not extra sustained throughput: under sustained overload the queue fills and the read loop applies backpressure as before. - Buffering adds a small amount of processing latency and memory proportional to queue depth. ### Additional Notes Implementation follows the existing perf map reorderer: the dispatcher is tied to the probe context and `WaitGroup` for clean shutdown, and records are passed by pointer and returned to the pool after processing to avoid a per-event copy. Draft: opened for early review; release note and tests still to add. Made with [Cursor](https://cursor.com)

signals.title: fix(e2e): CentOS 7 yum vault mirrors
signals.text: <!-- dd-meta {"pullId":"a1690776-5acc-42ba-b967-8f9ed1ebf680","source":"chat","resourceId":"3ccc3ce3-feac-4128-956d-32085850139b","workflowId":"033bd140-0f89-4a0a-9a1b-d6aa324a0839","codeChangeId":"033bd140-0f89-4a0a-9a1b-d6aa324a0839","sourceType":"slack"} --> ### What does this PR do? Fixes CentOS 7 E2E jobs on `main` that are red because the OS is EOL. On CentOS 7 the stock `/centos/7/` path on `vault.centos.org` now returns `HTTP 403`, so any `yum` transaction that must refresh the `base`/`updates`/`extras` metadata fails with `No more mirrors to try`. See incident-59302 Two jobs are affected today: - `new-e2e-installer` — `(*Host).InstallDocker()` runs `sudo yum install -y docker`; docker never installs and the failure surfaces confusingly as the cleanup defer's `systemctl start docker` → **"Failed to start docker.service: Unit not found."** - `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-centos-a7-x86_64` (incident 59303) — `sudo yum install -y datadog-agent-ddot` fails refreshing the same CentOS base repo. This adds `(*Host).ConfigureYumMirrors()` in `test/new-e2e/tests/installer/host/host.go`, the yum-side counterpart to the existing `ConfigureAptMirrors()`. On CentOS 7 it rewrites `/etc/yum.repos.d/CentOS-Base.repo` so `base`/`updates`/`extras` each list three baseurls with `failovermethod=priority`, tried in order: 1. `http://vault.centos.org/7.9.2009/{os,updates,extras}/$basearch/` — canonical archive (primary) 2. `https://linuxsoft.cern.ch/centos-vault/7.9.2009/...` — CERN mirror (fallback) 3. `https://archive.kernel.org/centos-vault/7.9.2009/...` — kernel.org mirror (fallback) plus `skip_if_unavailable=1` and `timeout=30` (fail fast / degrade gracefully instead of hanging until the 2h job timeout), `gpgcheck=1` against the on-box CentOS-7 key, then `yum clean all`. Explicit baseurls are required because the old `mirror.centos.org` / `mirrorlist.centos.org` services were removed at EOL, so a mirrorlist is not an option. It is called from each suite's `SetupSuite`, before the first yum operation: - `test/new-e2e/tests/installer/unix/all_packages_test.go` and `.../script/all_scripts_test.go` (job `new-e2e-installer`) - `test/new-e2e/tests/agent-platform/tests/ddot_install_test.go` (job `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-centos-a7-x86_64`) — this suite already builds an `installer/host.Host`, so the fix is reused as-is. The helper is guarded to `Flavor == CentOS && Version starts with "7"`, so it no-ops on RHEL/Amazon Linux and on the CentOS 6 jobs (which use a different vault tree). We keep using `vault.centos.org` (the correct registry for EOL CentOS); `InstallDocker()` and the ddot install path are otherwise unchanged. ### Motivation Both jobs are red on `main`, and both root-cause to the same external event: CentOS 7 EOL / `vault.centos.org` returning 403 on the `/centos/7/` path, so every run fails regardless of the commit. The earlier apt-mirror hardening (#54459) had no yum/CentOS equivalent — this closes that gap and covers the agent-platform ddot suite that shares the same `Host` helper. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Confirmed the failure signature via CI: `new-e2e-installer` jobs (`1945363716`, `1944844242`, `1945267523`) and `new-e2e-agent-platform-ddot-centos-a7-x86_64` jobs (as recent as 2026-08-17) all show `CentOS-7 - Base` / `HTTPS Error 403 - Forbidden` / `No more mirrors to try` on `centos_79`. - Chose the primary URL from in-repo precedent: `pkg/util/kernel/headers/download/rpm/centos.go` uses the same `http://vault.centos.org/7.9.2009/{os,updates}/$basearch/` path in production (hence `http` + gpgcheck against the on-box key). - Verified the CERN and kernel.org fallbacks are the external mirrors listed on `vault.centos.org`'s own index and mirror the full `7.9.2009/` tree (paths map directly). They sit behind vault via `failovermethod=priority`; they are best-effort, not SLA-backed. - Verified the affected suites explicitly opt into internet via `ec2.WithInternetAccess()`, so the archives are reachable during setup. - Scoped via a `Flavor == CentOS && Version` prefix guard; confirmed no new imports, no BUILD.bazel changes, gofmt-safe indentation, balanced braces, and that `InstallDocker()` is byte-identical to `main`. - A local compile/lint check and a live reachability probe were not possible in this sandbox (pinned Go toolchain unavailable; outbound to vault blocked). The affected E2E jobs are the end-to-end validators. ### Additional Notes - Not covered here (same root cause, larger change): `new-e2e-agent-platform-step-by-step-centos-a7-x86_64` is also failing, but `stepByStepSuite` does not use `installer/host` and would need extra plumbing to call the helper. The `rpm-centos6` job is CentOS 6 (different vault tree) and is intentionally excluded by the version guard. Happy to extend to step-by-step in a follow-up or here if desired. - Because CentOS 7 vault content is frozen (no further security updates), the robust long-term fix is a one-time `reposync` of the tree into an owned artifact store (Artifactory/S3/Pulp, ~50 GB) with the fleet pointed at that — out of scope here, noted for follow-up. - Residual gap worth a reviewer's eye: the in-repo production reference exercises `/os/` and `/updates/`; `/extras/` (which provides the `docker` package) is part of the same `7.9.2009` tree but isn't independently proven in-repo — CI will confirm. --- PR by Bits - [View session in Datadog](https://app.datadoghq.com/code/3ccc3ce3-feac-4128-956d-32085850139b) Comment @datadog to request changes

signals.title: [CONTP-1925] fix(ad): skip prometheus service checks with kubernetes_container_names
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Skips Cluster Agent prometheus service and endpoint checks when a prometheus scrape config sets `kubernetes_container_names`. Adds `HasContainerNamesFilter()` and applies the skip in both `prometheus_services` and `prometheus_services_eps`. ### Motivation Fixes [CONTP-1925](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONTP-1925). The Node Agent already filters prometheus pod checks by container name, but the Cluster Agent only matched service annotations. That let service-level openmetrics checks get scheduled and dispatched to node agents even when no matching container existed. Container name filtering is pod-level, so the Cluster Agent should not handle those configs. ### Describe how you validated your changes **Unit tests** - `prometheus_services_test.go` - `prometheus_services_eps_test.go` - `prometheus_test.go` **Manual test on kind** Deploy the Agent with a custom prometheus scrape config that filters on container name: ```yaml datadog: clusterName: contp1925 clusterChecks: enabled: true prometheusScrape: enabled: true serviceEndpoints: true version: 2 additionalConfigs: - autodiscovery: kubernetes_container_names: - example-container configurations: - namespace: example metrics: - .* clusterAgent: image: repository: contp1925-dca tag: local pullPolicy: Never ``` Deploy a test pod and service with `prometheus.io/scrape: "true"` but a non-matching container name: ```yaml apiVersion: v1 kind: Pod metadata: name: example-openmetrics annotations: prometheus.io/scrape: "true" prometheus.io/port: "8888" prometheus.io/path: "/metrics" spec: containers: - name: wrong-container-name image: prom/node-exporter:v1.8.2 args: ["--web.listen-address=:8888"] --- apiVersion: v1 kind: Service metadata: name: example-openmetrics annotations: prometheus.io/scrape: "true" prometheus.io/port: "8888" prometheus.io/path: "/metrics" spec: selector: app: example-openmetrics ports: - port: 8888 targetPort: 8888 ``` Verify no openmetrics check is scheduled for `example-openmetrics` ```bash kubectl exec <cluster-agent-pod> -- agent clusterchecks ``` ```bash kubectl exec <agent-pod> -c agent -- agent configcheck | grep openmetrics ``` Expected: no openmetrics check for the non-matching pod. Deploy a positive control pod with the matching container name `example-container` and confirm the Node Agent still schedules the check via `prometheus-pods`, while the Cluster Agent still does not schedule a service-level check. [CONTP-1925]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CONTP-1925?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signals.title: feat(dogstatsd): detect client payload drops
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Detects sustained DogStatsD client-reported payload-byte drops for UDS and UDS-stream clients using telemetry from the normal final aggregation path. When the drop rate exceeds 1%, the Agent reports a per-Agent Agent Health issue containing queue, writer, and unclassified drop totals. The issue resolves after sustained healthy telemetry. This adds two confirmation-period settings: - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.unhealthy_confirmation_window` defaults to `1m` and prevents transient drops from opening an issue. - `dogstatsd_client_drop_detection.recovery_confirmation_window` defaults to `30m` and prevents intermittent drops from repeatedly resolving and reopening the issue. ### Motivation This builds on #54381, which exposes DogStatsD client byte telemetry through Agent Telemetry/COAT. Detecting sustained drops in the Agent provides consistent behavior across supported clients and surfaces an actionable Agent Health issue without requiring new client payloads or library changes. ### Describe how you validated your changes - Unit tests covering detection, confirmation, recovery, missing telemetry, restart reconciliation, and multi-worker flush ordering - Fakeintake integration test covering ACTIVE and RESOLVED Agent Health reports - Updated the benchmarks ### Additional Notes

signals.title: feat(ndm): add the workloadbalancing component
signals.text: ## What New `comp/workloadbalancing` component. Subscribes to the shared `HA_AGENT` Remote Config product for per-device workload balancing assignments, distinguished from HA Agent's own documents by an explicit `type` field. - **Registration is unconditional**: it always listens on `HA_AGENT` and reports apply status for its own documents, independent of the local `agent_workload_balancing.enabled` flag. That flag only gates `IsGroupActive`'s effect — nothing calls it yet, that's a following PR. - **Fallback owner**: when `comp/haagent` is disabled on an agent, `comp/workloadbalancing` reports status for anything that doesn't match its own discriminator too, so a document is never silently dropped by both sides. - **Malformed-but-present documents**: reported as an apply-status error *and* keep the group's previous assignment rather than clearing it, since "malformed" isn't the same as "removed." - Wired only into the three binaries that actually run the check-execution worker pool `IsGroupActive` will gate: `cmd/agent/subcommands/run`, `cmd/cluster-agent/subcommands/start`, and `cmd/cluster-agent-cloudfoundry/subcommands/run`. Not `diagnose`, `flare`, `jmx`, `snmp`, `check`, `dogstatsd`, `serverless-init`, or `systray`: none of those run checks through that worker pool, so there's nothing for the component to do there. ## Not in scope here - Nothing reads `IsGroupActive` yet — no effect on check execution until the worker-gating PR. - SNMP's instance-level config field, metric emission, and inventory metadata are separate, following PRs. - The RC schema itself lives in `dd-source`, coordinated separately. ## Testing Unit tests cover: valid assignment (active/standby), malformed-but-present (error + keeps prior state), fallback-owner both ways (HA Agent enabled/disabled), the local flag being off (document still claimed and reported, `IsGroupActive` still `true`), a group's assignment clearing once its document stops appearing in a later poll, and the RC listener always registering regardless of the local flag. > **Note:** This PR was created by Claude

signals.title: Enables the v3 metrics intake for series in DDOT
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Enables the **v3 metrics intake for series** in DDOT (the `otel-agent` binary). Also included: - Updates two guard tests (`compression_consistency_test.go`, `agent_config_test.go`): `"false"` → `"datadog_only"`, and refreshes a now-stale comment (`otel-agent forces zlib`, obsolete since DDOT moved to zstd). - A new e2e test `test/new-e2e/tests/otel/otel-agent/v3_series_test.go` that provisions DDOT with v3 enabled and asserts series are routed to the v3 endpoint and shipped zstd. ### Motivation OTAGENT-1130, under epic OTAGENT-1133 ("Reduce customer metrics egress bandwidth 30–50% with v3 payload"). DDOT was the last OTel surface still on the v2 series intake. It was blocked because v3 requires zstd and DDOT forced zlib; #52758 switched DDOT to zstd for all signals, removing the blocker. This PR moves DDOT onto the v3 series path, aligning it with the core Agent (series v3 default since 7.81). The exporter's default translator still performs cumulative→delta for monotonic sums, so this works on the current mapper; the `cumulativetodelta` converter (OTAGENT-1128, already merged) is complementary, not a prerequisite. ### Describe how you validated your changes - **Unit:** `cmd/otel-agent/config` tests pass; the guard tests now assert the resolved value is `datadog_only`. - **Static:** `dda inv linter.go` — 0 issues; `dda inv otel-agent.build` — OK. - **Manual (local, standalone otel-agent → fakeintake, `DD_USE_V3_API_SERIES_ENABLED=true`, zstd):** series routed to `/api/intake/metrics/v3/series` and **0** on `/api/v2/series`; all payloads zstd (wire magic `28b52ffd`); v3 payloads decode correctly; a cumulative Sum arrived as a delta `COUNT` (c2d); sketches stayed on `/api/beta/sketches` (v2). - **E2E:** new `TestOTelAgentV3Series` (KinD DDOT with v3 enabled) asserts OTLP metrics reach the intake, series land on the v3 endpoint (`RouteStats`), and v3 payloads are zstd. Auto-wired into the `new-e2e-otel` job — no CI changes. (Runs in CI on this PR.) ### Additional Notes - **Kill-switch / rollout:** enablement follows `use_v3_api.series.enabled` (default `datadog_only`). v2 remains the compat/fallback path (non-Datadog destinations, non-zstd builds, non-migrated regions). Opt out with `use_v3_api.series.enabled=false` (or `DD_USE_V3_API_SERIES_ENABLED=false`). - **Scope:** series only. Sketches (distributions) stay on v2 (v3 for sketches is a separate opt-in). - **Known follow-up (this PR):** the auto-injected `datadog/dd-autoconfigured` flare extension keeps its own zlib serializer and now logs a benign but misleading "disabling v3 metrics intake" warning — the same warning #52301 suppressed on the OSS path, surfaced because v3 is now enabled in-process. Egress is unaffected (verified v3 + zstd); the warning does not reflect the actual series path. To be addressed. - this deliberately does **not** revert #52301 (`serializerexporter/serializer.go`). That line only runs for the OSS Datadog exporter in opentelemetry-collector-contrib https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/OTAGENT-1130

signals.title: [BARX-2009] Drop Agent 6 RC tags on Go modules
signals.text: ## Motivation - Agent releases create a nested Go module tag for every release candidate. These tags significantly increase the repository's tag count and add pressure to GitHub and GitLab. Agent 7 already drops creating these RC module tags; this PR applies the same behavior to Agent 6. See the [RFC](https://docs.google.com/document/d/15XFZ4AKy8Yhyruo7zilTR84j5kV1dI5eFBhoEFfGzhI/edit?tab=t.0) for more info. ## Important Note - Agent 6 RC module dependencies use versions backed by RC tags. After removing those tags, the dependencies must use another resolvable version. We use pseudo-versions derived from the release branch commit, ensuring modules in the same RC can consume each other’s changes without creating nested RC tags. ## Changes - Skip nested Go module tag creation for Agent 6 release candidates. - Resolve Agent 6 RC internal module dependencies to canonical pseudo-versions at the current release branch commit. - Cache each resolved pseudo-version while updating module requirements. - Keep final Agent 6 release tags - Document the Agent 6 RC pseudo-version workflow. - Add unit coverage for tag suppression and pseudo-version dependency updates. ## Tests - `dda inv invoke-unit-tests.run --tests=release` (46 tests passed) - `GITLAB_CI=true dda inv linter.python` - `git diff --check`

signals.title: [NETPATH-873] include config name in netpath payloads
signals.text: [AI] ### What does this PR do? - Reads `test_config_name` from scheduled and dynamic `NETWORK_PATH` Remote Configuration documents. - Propagates the name alongside `test_config_id` through scheduled checks and dynamic path attribution. - Adds `test_config_name` to Network Path intake payloads when a name is available and verifies it in unit and E2E coverage. - Continues accepting legacy RC documents that do not contain a config name. ### Motivation Network Path configuration names are currently unavailable to the Agent, so emitted traceroute results can identify a configuration only by ID. The corresponding [dd-source change](https://github.com/ddoghq/dd-source/pull/57975) adds the user-facing name to Agent RC content as `test_config_name`. Propagating that value into NetPath payloads lets the backend associate each result with the configuration name while preserving compatibility with configurations created before the rollout. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `bazel test //comp/core/autodiscovery/providers/networkpath:networkpath_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl:impl_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/common:common_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/connfilter:connfilter_test //comp/networkpath/npcollector/impl/pathteststore:pathteststore_test //comp/syntheticstestscheduler/impl:impl_test //pkg/collector/corechecks/networkpath:networkpath_test //pkg/networkpath/payload:payload_test` - `bazel build //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/dynamic-tests:dynamic-tests_test //test/new-e2e/tests/netpath/network-path-integration:network-path-integration_test` ### Additional Notes The Agent intentionally treats `test_config_name` as optional during ingestion so existing stored RC documents remain valid during rollout. Empty names are omitted from emitted payloads, preserving the existing payload shape for legacy and unmanaged producers.

signals.title: [WINA-3031] Upgrade datadog-go to v5.9.1
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? - Upgrades `github.com/DataDog/datadog-go/v5` from `v5.9.0` to `v5.9.1` across the Go workspace. ### Motivation [#incident-59243](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0BQAB1T274) https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3031 `datadog-go v5.9.1` fixes a nil pointer dereference in the Windows named-pipe writer (DataDog/datadog-go#397). The pipe connection is established on first write, so closing a client that never successfully wrote dereferenced a nil `net.Conn` and terminated the process. The Agent Data Plane pre-flight probe triggers this on Windows. It dials the pipe once to prove readiness, then the statsd client dials again on its first write; when that second dial loses a startup race, the deferred `client.Close()` crashed the Agent service with `0xc0000005`. This is intermittent by nature — it needs the first dial to succeed and the second to fail. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go list -m github.com/DataDog/datadog-go/v5` resolves to `v5.9.1`. - `go mod verify` — all modules verified. - `GOOS=windows go build ./comp/dataplane/...` passes. The fix is in a `//go:build windows` file, so a native build would not exercise it. - Confirmed every changed `go.mod`/`go.sum` line is datadog-go and nothing else. ### Additional Notes Renovate normally owns this bump (it did v5.9.0 in #53234), but `minimumReleaseAge: 7 days` means it would not open a PR until ~2026-08-24. Landing it manually since the crash blocks 7.84. The diff matches Renovate's output file-for-file, so it will simply see the dependency as current.

signals.title: Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signals.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process does not resolve secret-backend handles, provide the api_key as a plain value or enable config sync from the core agent (agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval) ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.

signals.title: trace/api: forward DD-EVP-ORIGIN and DD-EVP-ORIGIN-VERSION through EVP proxy
signals.text: ## Summary Add `DD-EVP-ORIGIN` and `DD-EVP-ORIGIN-VERSION` to `EvpProxyAllowedHeaders` in `pkg/trace/api/evp_proxy.go` so server SDK metadata (SDK name and version) survives forwarding to Event Platform intake. Previously these headers were stripped by the allowlist, losing caller-supplied origin identity at the Agent even when the SDK sent them. Closes [FFL-3014](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FFL-3014). ## Why the general allowlist (not flagevaluation-specific) There is a single shared EVP proxy handler: `/evp_proxy/v1/`–`/v4/` all route to the same `evpProxyHandler` → `evpProxyForwarder` → `evpProxyTransport.RoundTrip`, which applies `EvpProxyAllowedHeaders` uniformly. There is no path-specific branching, so flagevaluation (`/evp_proxy/v2/api/v2/flagevaluation`) hits the exact same code path as every other EVP-proxied destination. This change therefore affects **all** EVP proxy traffic, not just the Feature Flags & Experimentation team's. This is intentional and we discuss tradeoffs below. ## Tradeoff considerations **Why we feel the blast radius is low:** - **Purely additive.** Headers are only forwarded *if the caller sends them*. - **Consistent with existing posture.** The allowlist already relays caller-supplied identity headers verbatim (`User-Agent`, `DD-CI-PROVIDER-NAME`). Adding origin/version is the same kind of operation: "relay what the caller sent" - **`DD-EVP-ORIGIN` is a general EVP convention, not an FFL-specific concept.** The agent itself sets it on its own outbound EVP calls (the logs, dyninst, and otel paths set it too). Letting it pass through the proxy is consistent with how the rest of the platform treats the header. - The Agent never invents these values, it only relays what the SDK sent. A rogue/unrelated client that doesn't send them is unaffected. **One thing worth flagging:** If any *other* EVP consumer were relying on these headers being **stripped** at the agent (e.g., to prevent clients from spoofing origin identity upstream), this change would loosen that guarantee. We assessed this as a non-issue: the current allowlist already forwards `User-Agent` and `DD-CI-PROVIDER-NAME` from callers, so "relay caller-supplied identity headers" is already the established posture, and there is no evidence any consumer depends on `DD-EVP-ORIGIN` being dropped. If such a consumer is later identified, the fix would be to gate forwarding on `req.URL.Path` but that additional complexity is not needed today. ## Test strategy - All tests use the existing `sendRequestThroughForwarderWithMockRoundTripper` harness (mock round-tripper captures outbound requests). No new infrastructure. ## Acceptance criteria (from FFL-3014) - [x] Captured outbound requests contain the exact incoming origin and version values. - [x] Existing EVP proxy tests pass. - [x] No request payload is modified (only headers). [FFL-3014]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FFL-3014?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: trace/api: forward DD-EVP-ORIGIN and DD-EVP-ORIGIN-VERSION through EVP proxy
signal.text: ## Summary Add `DD-EVP-ORIGIN` and `DD-EVP-ORIGIN-VERSION` to `EvpProxyAllowedHeaders` in `pkg/trace/api/evp_proxy.go` so server SDK metadata (SDK name and version) survives forwarding to Event Platform intake. Previously these headers were stripped by the allowlist, losing caller-supplied origin identity at the Agent even when the SDK sent them. Closes [FFL-3014](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FFL-3014). ## Why the general allowlist (not flagevaluation-specific) There is a single shared EVP proxy handler: `/evp_proxy/v1/`–`/v4/` all route to the same `evpProxyHandler` → `evpProxyForwarder` → `evpProxyTransport.RoundTrip`, which applies `EvpProxyAllowedHeaders` uniformly. There is no path-specific branching, so flagevaluation (`/evp_proxy/v2/api/v2/flagevaluation`) hits the exact same code path as every other EVP-proxied destination. This change therefore affects **all** EVP proxy traffic, not just the Feature Flags & Experimentation team's. This is intentional and we discuss tradeoffs below. ## Tradeoff considerations **Why we feel the blast radius is low:** - **Purely additive.** Headers are only forwarded *if the caller sends them*. - **Consistent with existing posture.** The allowlist already relays caller-supplied identity headers verbatim (`User-Agent`, `DD-CI-PROVIDER-NAME`). Adding origin/version is the same kind of operation: "relay what the caller sent" - **`DD-EVP-ORIGIN` is a general EVP convention, not an FFL-specific concept.** The agent itself sets it on its own outbound EVP calls (the logs, dyninst, and otel paths set it too). Letting it pass through the proxy is consistent with how the rest of the platform treats the header. - The Agent never invents these values, it only relays what the SDK sent. A rogue/unrelated client that doesn't send them is unaffected. **One thing worth flagging:** If any *other* EVP consumer were relying on these headers being **stripped** at the agent (e.g., to prevent clients from spoofing origin identity upstream), this change would loosen that guarantee. We assessed this as a non-issue: the current allowlist already forwards `User-Agent` and `DD-CI-PROVIDER-NAME` from callers, so "relay caller-supplied identity headers" is already the established posture, and there is no evidence any consumer depends on `DD-EVP-ORIGIN` being dropped. If such a consumer is later identified, the fix would be to gate forwarding on `req.URL.Path` but that additional complexity is not needed today. ## Test strategy - All tests use the existing `sendRequestThroughForwarderWithMockRoundTripper` harness (mock round-tripper captures outbound requests). No new infrastructure. ## Acceptance criteria (from FFL-3014) - [x] Captured outbound requests contain the exact incoming origin and version values. - [x] Existing EVP proxy tests pass. - [x] No request payload is modified (only headers). [FFL-3014]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/FFL-3014?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: fix(logs): protect PublicJSON from racing with SetTailingMode
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on `LogsConfig.TailingMode`: `PublicJSON()` was called on `*LogsConfig` directly without the `LogSource` lock, racing with `SetTailingMode()` which writes `Config.TailingMode` under the lock. signal.title: fix(serverless-init): eliminate GlobalTags data race in MicroVM trace tags
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Stops MicroVM's async `/run` lifecycle hook from mutating `Agent.GlobalTags` and routes the dynamic `lambda_microvm_id` tag update through the (already serverless-owned) span modifier instead. Concretely: - `pkg/serverless/trace/span_modifier.go`: `tags` field is now `atomic.Pointer[map[string]string]` (using `go.uber.org/atomic`, per repo convention); `ModifySpan` applies each tag lock-free via `Load()`. - `pkg/serverless/trace/trace.go`: adds `UpdateRuntimeTags`, which updates only the span modifier — never `GlobalTags`. The existing `SetTags` (called once, synchronously, at startup before the trace agent runs) is untouched and still updates both. - `cmd/serverless-init/main.go`: the two async `TraceTagSetterFunc` closures wired into the MicroVM lifecycle server now call `UpdateRuntimeTags` instead of `SetTags`. - `cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle/server.go`: updated a doc comment that named the (now stale) method satisfying `TraceTagSetter`. ### Motivation Codex flagged a data race on #53036: `serverlessTraceAgent.SetTags` is invoked from a goroutine inside the MicroVM lifecycle server's `/run` handler, which runs concurrently with the trace agent's span-processing loop. `SetTags` calls `Agent.SetGlobalTagsUnsafe`, whose own doc comment says "Unsafe for concurrent use" — it does a bare `a.conf.GlobalTags = tags` write, while `pkg/trace/agent/agent.go` (hot path, lines 531/711) and `pkg/trace/api/telemetry.go` read `a.conf.GlobalTags` with no synchronization at all. `GlobalTags` is computed once at config-build time, before the trace agent starts running, and every one of those readers assumes that invariant holds forever — MicroVM's dynamic per-invocation tag update is the only thing in the codebase that breaks it. In practice the write is a pointer swap to a new map rather than an in-place mutation, so the realistic worst case is a span in flight at the moment of the swap missing `lambda_microvm_id` — not a crash. But it's a genuine data race under the Go memory model: `go test -race` / `bazel test --config=race` will flag it the moment a concurrent test exercises this path, and nothing guarantees it stays benign under future compiler optimizations. The fix avoids touching any code shared with the non-serverless trace agent (`pkg/trace/agent`, `pkg/trace/api`, `pkg/trace/config`) by reusing `SpanModifier`, which already runs at the identical point in `agent.go`'s span-processing loop (right after the `GlobalTags` loop) and is exclusively serverless-owned. Its `tags` field existed before this change but was dead code — written by `SetTags`, never read by `ModifySpan`; this fix makes it real. This is scoped entirely to MicroVM. Every other cloud service (`AppService`, `CloudRun`, `ContainerApp`, `CloudRunJobs`) ignores `LifecycleCtx` in `Init`, so they never invoke the async closures — they only ever call the original, still-synchronous `SetTags` once at startup, unchanged by this PR. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added regression coverage for every change (7 new/extended tests): - `TestSpanModifierSetTagsConcurrentWithModifySpan` — hammers `SetTags`/`ModifySpan` from two goroutines under the race detector; this is the actual bug repro. - `TestSpanModifierModifySpanBeforeSetTags`, `...AppliesTagsSetDynamically`, `...ReflectsLatestSetTags` — functional coverage of the new atomic-pointer-backed tag application. - `TestServerlessTraceAgentSetTagsUpdatesGlobalTagsAndSpanModifier` — confirms the untouched synchronous `SetTags` path still updates both `GlobalTags` and the span modifier. - `TestServerlessTraceAgentUpdateRuntimeTagsDoesNotTouchGlobalTags` — the core assertion: `UpdateRuntimeTags` never writes `GlobalTags`. - `TestServerlessTraceAgentUpdateRuntimeTagsNoSpanModifier` — no-op safety when `SpanModifier` doesn't implement `taggable`. - Extended `TestSetupWithoutAPIKey` to also exercise `noopTraceAgent.UpdateRuntimeTags`. Run locally with: ```sh dda inv test --targets=./pkg/serverless/trace,./cmd/serverless-init,./cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle,./cmd/serverless-init/cloudservice --race dda inv linter.go --targets=./pkg/serverless/trace,./cmd/serverless-init,./cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle,./cmd/serverless-init/cloudservice ``` All 302 tests pass (4 skipped, platform-gated) with the race detector enabled; linter reports 0 issues. ### Additional Notes Stacked on #53096 (`tianning.li/microvm-07-05-main-wiring`) — base branch will move to `main` once that merges. `BUILD.bazel` files were checked (`bazel run //:gazelle -- update` + buildifier on the one Gazelle-managed directory touched, `cmd/serverless-init/lifecycle`); no changes needed since the rest of the touched files are under pre-existing `gazelle:exclude` directives (not yet Bazel-migrated). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

signal.title: fix(autoscaling/workload): fix data race on processor state in reconcile
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on `autoscalingValuesProcessor.state` and `autoscalingSettingsProcessor.state`: `reconcile()` read `p.state` without holding `updateLock` (in the nil check before `TryLock`), racing with `postProcess()` which writes `p.state` under the lock. signal.title: [WINA-3031] Upgrade datadog-go to v5.9.1
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? - Upgrades `github.com/DataDog/datadog-go/v5` from `v5.9.0` to `v5.9.1` across the Go workspace. ### Motivation [#incident-59243](https://dd.enterprise.slack.com/archives/C0BQAB1T274) https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/WINA-3031 `datadog-go v5.9.1` fixes a nil pointer dereference in the Windows named-pipe writer (DataDog/datadog-go#397). The pipe connection is established on first write, so closing a client that never successfully wrote dereferenced a nil `net.Conn` and terminated the process. The Agent Data Plane pre-flight probe triggers this on Windows. It dials the pipe once to prove readiness, then the statsd client dials again on its first write; when that second dial loses a startup race, the deferred `client.Close()` crashed the Agent service with `0xc0000005`. This is intermittent by nature — it needs the first dial to succeed and the second to fail. ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go list -m github.com/DataDog/datadog-go/v5` resolves to `v5.9.1`. - `go mod verify` — all modules verified. - `GOOS=windows go build ./comp/dataplane/...` passes. The fix is in a `//go:build windows` file, so a native build would not exercise it. - Confirmed every changed `go.mod`/`go.sum` line is datadog-go and nothing else. ### Additional Notes Renovate normally owns this bump (it did v5.9.0 in #53234), but `minimumReleaseAge: 7 days` means it would not open a PR until ~2026-08-24. Landing it manually since the crash blocks 7.84. The diff matches Renovate's output file-for-file, so it will simply see the dependency as current.

signal.title: test(network/usm): run the USM and classification suites on the fentry tracer
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Runs the USM and protocol-classification test suites against the **fentry** connection tracer, which they previously never exercised. Fentry was absent from `usmtestutil.SupportedBuildModes`, and three separate gates short-circuited on it even when it was selected: | Gate | Old behavior on fentry | |---|---| | `httpSupported()` / `httpsSupported()` (`usm/tests`) | returned `false` → suites skipped | | `setupTracer` (`tracer_classification_test.go`) | force-disabled `ProtocolClassificationEnabled` | | `TestTLSClassification` | `t.Skip("protocol classification not supported for fentry tracer")` | The hardcoded gates are replaced with real capability queries: `classificationSupported` now dispatches to the fentry or kprobe tracer as appropriate. To make that possible, `fentry.classificationSupported` is exported as `ClassificationSupported`, matching kprobe's existing export. That rename is the only non-test change here and carries no behavior change; its sole caller, `initFentryTracer`, is updated. `httpSupported()` in `pkg/network/tracer` also had a fentry early-return, which this PR removes. `usmtestutil.SupportedBuildModes` is split rather than extended. Fentry is only meaningful for tests that construct a connection tracer. The new `SupportedBuildModesWithFentry()` is used only by `pkg/network/usm/tests`. ### Motivation Part of the fentry tracer cleanup and validation effort. The fentry tracer supports protocol classification in production, but no USM test ever ran against it, so that support was unverified. ### Describe how you validated your changes Run on ubuntu-24 / 6.8.0-86 with `TEST_FENTRY_OVERRIDE=true` (this kernel carries the AUTOSEL backport of the RCU-exit deadlock fix, so it runs fentry despite being below the `kv >= 6.9` test gate). - **`TestUSMSuite/fentry`** — all 7 suite methods pass, across 3 full-suite runs. - **`TestTracerSuite/fentry`** — 109 pass, 5 skip, 0 fail. - **`TestGetStats`** — passes on fentry. Its USM assertion is dead code and this PR does not change that, but verified against the follow-up branch that repairs it: with both applied, `TestGetStats` asserts the USM telemetry section on fentry and passes on both `ebpf_conntracker` variants, so fentry does genuinely build a USM monitor and report its telemetry.

signal.title: fix(kubestatemetrics): serialize access to shared availableStores map
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on the kube-state-metrics library's package-level `availableStores` map: `WithCustomResourceStoreFactories` and `BuildStores` mutate/read this shared map without synchronization, so two concurrent KSM check workers calling `buildStores()` race on it. Adds a package-level mutex (`ksmBuilderMu`) that serializes access to both methods. ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `TestWithCustomResourceStoreFactoriesConcurrent` which calls `WithCustomResourceStoreFactories` concurrently on 100 goroutines; it reproduces the race under `-race` before the fix and is clean after (`dda inv test --targets=./pkg/kubestatemetrics/builder/... --race`).

signal.title: Reject unresolved secret handles on the NPM direct-send path
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds `endpoint.CheckAPIKeysResolved` and calls it from `sender.New` (`pkg/network/sender/sender_linux.go`), so that when `network_config.direct_send` is enabled and `api_key` is still an unresolved `ENC[...]` secret handle, the NPM direct sender refuses to start and says why: ``` error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ("ENC[...]"): this process does not resolve secret-backend handles, provide the api_key as a plain value or enable config sync from the core agent (agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval) ``` The check also covers `process_config.additional_endpoints`, since those keys come from the same config and are equally likely to be secret-backed. ### Motivation NTWK-817. A customer set `api_key` via the secret backend (`ENC[k8s_secret@...]`) and enabled `network_config.direct_send`. CNM data never arrived, and nothing in the logs pointed at the cause. What was happening: system-probe wires the **no-op** secrets component (`secretsnoopfx.Module()` in `cmd/system-probe/subcommands/run/command.go`), so it cannot resolve secret handles itself. It only ever receives resolved values from the core agent over config sync (`comp/core/configsync`)— both `agent_ipc.config_refresh_interval` and `agent_ipc.port` default to `0` (`pkg/config/setup/all_settings.go`). With config sync off, `config.GetString("api_key")` returned the literal string `ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, and the direct sender passed it straight through as the `Dd-Api-Key` header. Every payload was rejected by the intake, and because the direct sender has no API-key validation (`DisableAPIKeyChecking = true`) there was no error identifying the key as the problem. Silent data loss. This does not make the customer's setup work — it makes the failure legible. The configuration they still need is in the section below. ### Scope of the check, and why it is not in `GetAPIEndpoints` The check is deliberately **not** inside `GetAPIEndpoints`, even though that is where the API key is read. `module.FactoryDependencies` (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/common.go`) declares `ConnectionsForwarder connectionsforwarder.Component` as a **non-optional** field, and `startSystemProbe` takes that struct — so Fx constructs `connectionsforwarder` on **every** system-probe start regardless of `direct_send`, and its constructor calls `GetAPIEndpoints` and propagates the error (`comp/forwarder/connectionsforwarder/impl/connectionsforwarder.go`). Putting the check there made any system-probe with a secret-backed `api_key` fail to boot outright, taking CWS, USM, and discovery with it — a regression for a large existing population, since that construction was previously a harmless no-op (a forwarder built with an unusable key that nothing read). Keeping the check at the `sender.New` call site means the failure is confined to what is actually broken: the module loader logs the error and skips `network_tracer`, and the rest of system-probe runs normally (`pkg/system-probe/api/module/loader.go`). NPM and USM are both lost, as they share the `network_tracer` module — unavoidable without silently falling back to the process-agent collection path, which would change the deployment topology in response to a config error. Graceful degradation was considered and rejected. `Register()` skips the `/connections` endpoint when `DirectSend` is true, so keeping the module alive without a sender would load eBPF programs, collect connections, and drop them all — the cost of NPM with none of the data, and quietly. ### Customer-facing configuration required for `direct_send` + secrets To make secret-backed `api_key` actually work with `direct_send`, config sync must be enabled so the core agent supplies the resolved value. In `datadog.yaml` (read by both the core agent and system-probe), either TCP: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 # seconds; must be > 0 port: 5008 # any free port ``` or, preferably in Kubernetes, over a socket: ```yaml agent_ipc: config_refresh_interval: 30 use_socket: true socket_path: /var/run/datadog/agent_ipc.socket # on a volume both containers mount ``` One of the two transports must be set. `comp/core/configsync/impl/module.go` logs `configsync disabled: ...` and does nothing if `config_refresh_interval <= 0`, or if `use_socket` is false and `port <= 0`. Caveats worth flagging to anyone enabling this: - **Startup becomes dependent on core-agent readiness.** system-probe runs config sync with `OnInitSync: true` and a **10-second** deadline (`configSyncTimeout`, retrying every 2s). If the core agent is not yet listening, system-probe fails to start with `failed to sync config at startup, is the core agent listening on '...'`. Where both start together this is a real race. - **`use_socket` needs a shared volume.** The standard Helm chart does not give the two containers a shared writable run directory by default; an explicit `emptyDir` mounted into both is required. - The only alternative is a literal `api_key` in the config system-probe reads, which defeats the point of using a secret backend. This interaction is currently undocumented — `direct_send` has no entry in `pkg/config/example/system-probe_*.yaml.example`, no description in the generated schema, and no coverage under `docs/`. Documentation is intentionally left out of this PR and will be handled separately. ### Describe how you validated your changes Unit: added `endpoints_test.go` covering a plain key, a bare handle, a whitespace-padded handle, a handle in an additional endpoint, and an empty key. `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/process/runner/endpoint` passes; `dda inv linter.go` clean on `pkg/process/runner/endpoint` and `pkg/network/sender`. End-to-end, in a Linux container (arm64, kernel 6.8, CO-RE) with `direct_send: true`, `api_key: ENC[k8s_secret@...]`, `process_config.process_dd_url` pointed at a local stub intake, and no config sync configured: | | before this change | with this change | |---|---|---| | system-probe process | runs but direct sender gets payloads rejected | stays up, socket bound | | `network_tracer` | n/a | `error creating module network_tracer: create direct sender: api_key is an unresolved secret handle ...` | | other modules | none | `discovery` and `event_monitor` both started | | requests reaching intake | payloads sent with `Dd-Api-Key: ENC[...]` | 0 | | `ENC[` observed on the wire | yes | 0 | `dda inv system-probe.build` also verified in the Linux container, since `sender_linux.go` is not compiled on macOS. ### Additional Notes The error message names the offending setting path, so it distinguishes `api_key` from `process_config.additional_endpoints`. The handle itself is included in the message; it is a reference, not a secret value.
signal.author: rahulkaukuntla

signal.title: fix(system-probe): protect module loader registry with mutex during Register
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Fixes a data race on the module loader registry: `Register` wrote `l.cfg`, `l.stats`, and iterated `l.modules` without holding the loader mutex, racing with `GetStats` which takes the lock. Added `l.Lock()` around the writes and snapshotted module entries before spawning stats goroutines. ### Motivation Fix a race, found via a race-detector-enabled build in staging (see #54333 for context). ### Describe how you validated your changes No unit test added — `Register` requires full eBPF factories, config, and dependencies that can't be constructed in a unit test, and duplicating the internal logic in a test wouldn't validate the actual fix. The race is eliminated by construction: all writes to the shared fields now go through the same mutex that `GetStats` already takes.

signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Adds an MVP rule to create Mac PKG files. - bazel/rules/macos/pkg/pkg_mac_pkg.bzl - materialize srcs to diesk via a pkg_install-generated installer. sub-optimal but equivalent to what omnibus does today. This is essentially temporary code. Future work will improve that. - bazel/rules/macos/pkg/build_mac_pkg.sh — the pkgbuild wrapper - Adds packages/agent/macos/BUILD.bazel, to create a .pkg file for datadog-agent. This is obviously incomplete because //cmd/agent:agent is not ready yet. - packages/agent/product/BUILD.bazel — fixed a pre-existing bug where //cmd/loader:trace_loader (Linux-only target_compatible_with) was listed unconditionally, breaking any non-Linux consumer of :all_files. ### Motivation ### Describe how you validated your changes Claude's used lsbom to verify that the pkg format was valid. Hand compare the DMG built from the omnibus job to this output. ``` $ tree_size_compare --save pkg.json bazel-bin/packages/agent/macos/pkg.pkg $ tree_size_compare --save=dmg.json $HOME/Downloads/datadog-agent-7.83.0-devel.git.371.359005d.pipeline.126858256-1.arm64.dmg $ grep PKG@ dmg.json | sed -e 's/@PKG@/opt\/datadog-agent/' >/tmp/dmg.files $ grep path pkg.json >/tmp/pkg.files $ grep system-prob /tmp/*.files /tmp/dmg.files: "path": "opt/datadog-agent/bin/agent/dist/system-probe.yaml", /tmp/dmg.files: "path": "opt/datadog-agent/embedded/bin/system-probe", /tmp/dmg.files: "path": "opt/datadog-agent/etc/system-probe.yaml", /tmp/dmg.files: "path": "opt/datadog-agent/etc/system-probe.yaml.example", /tmp/pkg.files: "path": "opt/datadog-agent/etc/system-probe.yaml", ``` The missing files are expected right now, because we have not done serious work at wiring up the dependencies. ### Future steps - tweak dependencies and config until we have fidelity with the omnibus packager. Brew the omnibus jobs to do this. - replace use of pkg_install to manifest the tree with a direct reader/writer. That is probably upstreamable to rules_pkg in a contrib section. - Eliminate materialize.py - Upstream change to pkg_install to allow installation to a tree artifact - Add that to a pkg_files group that gets the tree artifact and the pre/post install scripts. - Feed that to the package builder. - Add signing (blocked on ABLD-386)

signal.title: [DO NOT MERGE] One-off e2e run with ADP enabled by default
signal.text: ## Summary Temporarily flips \`data_plane.enabled\` from \`false\` to \`true\` in the agent's compiled-in config default so that every e2e test in the full suite runs against ADP without requiring per-test changes or test duplication. The change is throwaway — close without merging once the CI run completes. This is the same config knob used by the AMP ADP test helpers (DADP-72, see [Slack thread](https://dd.slack.com/archives/C070PQKLLP5/p1783453441368899)). ## How to kick off the full e2e suite Trigger a new pipeline on this branch and set the CI variable: \`\`\` RUN_E2E_TESTS=on \`\`\` That variable hits the \`if_run_all_e2e_tests\` rule in \`.gitlab-ci.yml\` and flips all e2e jobs from manual to \`on_success\`. ## CI findings (ADP 1.5.1, branch jszwedko/run-ci-adp-enabled) ### Fixed in this PR - **Windows MSI \`status_command_infos\`**: All MSI test variants fail because \`agent_behaviour.go\` asserts the status output contains "DogStatsD". When ADP handles DSD, the \`DogStatsD\` status section is absent (the \`EnabledInternal()\` guard prevents registering the status provider). Fixed by accepting either "DogStatsD" or "Dogstatsd Metric Sample" (always present in the Aggregator section). ### Known pre-existing failures (ADP limitations, tracked in Saluki) - **\`TestReplayWithTagEnrichment\`** — ADP doesn't enrich replayed DSD packets with current tagger state. Tracked in Saluki. ### New failures requiring Saluki fixes - **Container DSD tests (ECS \`TestDogtstatsdUDP\`, \`TestDogtstatsdUDS\`; Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods)**: In container environments (ECS, K8s/Kind), fakeintake is configured as \`DD_ADDITIONAL_ENDPOINTS\` rather than \`dd_url\`. ADP doesn't appear to forward DogStatsD metrics to \`additional_endpoints\`, so no metrics arrive at fakeintake. In VM tests where fakeintake IS \`dd_url\` (primary endpoint), DSD forwarding works. This points to an \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding gap in ADP. - The Kind \`dogstatsd-uds\` pods fail to become Ready — the workload pods mount \`/var/run/datadog/dsd.socket\` as a HostPath volume (type \`Socket\`). With ADP enabled, the core agent's DSD server doesn't start (so no socket is created); ADP must create it but apparently doesn't complete socket setup in time or at the expected path. - Root cause: ADP \`additional_endpoints\` forwarding — active Saluki config migration work (issues #2312–#2316) may be the upstream cause. ### Other failures under investigation - **Anomaly detection tests** — under investigation, may be ADP-independent - **GPU tests** — under investigation ## Test plan - No new tests. The goal is to observe which existing e2e tests break when ADP is the default. - \`new-e2e-amp-adp\` (existing) runs the AMP suite filtered to \`--run "ADP"\` tests; this PR covers the rest. **DO NOT MERGE** — this default flip must not land on \`main\`.

signal.title: [autoscaling] Expose DPA objective target metric
signal.text: <!-- dd-meta {"pullId":"00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000","source":"chat","resourceId":"f1899761-3730-41e5-bfad-a976d188b111","workflowId":"9b872e58-062a-40fb-983d-d269782737de","codeChangeId":"9b872e58-062a-40fb-983d-d269782737de","sourceType":"chat"} --> ### What does this PR do? Adds a new Cluster Agent gauge, `datadog.cluster_agent.autoscaling.workload.objective.target`, that exposes the target value configured in a `DatadogPodAutoscaler`'s `spec.objectives`. Previously the objective/target value (e.g. CPU `utilization: 70`) was only consumed internally by the external recommender request builder and the local replica calculator — it was never surfaced to users as a metric. The metric supports all three objective kinds and both value types, differentiated by tags: - `objective_type`: `pod_resource` | `container_resource` | `custom_query` - `value_type`: `utilization` | `absolute_value` - `objective_index`: 0-based position in `spec.objectives[]` - `resource_name`: `cpu` | `memory` (present for resource objectives; omitted for `custom_query`) - `kube_container_name`: present only for `container_resource` objectives `objective_index` guarantees a unique tag-set per objective so multiple objectives never collapse into a single timeseries in the metrics store (which would silently drop all but the last-sampled value on each flush). It is the only distinguishing tag for multiple `custom_query` objectives — which share every other tag — and also disambiguates the pathological case of two objectives targeting the same container and resource. This is forward-looking for multi-objective support. The index is positional: reordering/inserting an objective shifts the indices of later objectives (documented). Value units follow the conventions already used in this generator: - `utilization` → raw percentage (0–100) - `absolute_value` + `cpu` → millicores; + `memory` → bytes - `absolute_value` for `custom_query` → query-native float via `AsApproximateFloat64()` Changes: - `generator.go`: two helpers (`objectiveTags`, `objectiveValue`) and a new emission block iterating `spec.Objectives`; `objectiveTags` takes the loop index and emits an `objective_index` tag. The pre-existing status block's inline sub-numbering (`12a/b/c`) is renumbered to `14a/b/c` for consistency (comment-only). - `generator_test.go`: table cases covering pod/container/custom-query objectives, utilization and absolute values (cpu millicores, memory bytes, custom-query float), multiple objectives, the nil-value guard, and a dedicated case proving two `custom_query` objectives become distinct series via `objective_index`. - `metrics.md`: new "Autoscaling objectives (target values)" section documenting the metric, tags (including `objective_index`), and value-unit semantics. - `releasenotes-dca/notes/`: added a cluster-agent enhancement release note for the new metric. ### Motivation Users configure a scaling target (e.g. CPU utilization) via `spec.objectives` but had no way to observe that configured target in Datadog — making it impossible to graph the target alongside actual utilization/recommendations, or to alert when the configured objective drifts from what is expected. Exposing it as a gauge closes that gap and complements the existing constraints and status metrics. The `objective_index` tag ensures the schema is safe for the upcoming multi-objective use cases (e.g. several `ContainerResource` or `CustomQuery` objectives on one DPA). ### Describe how you validated your changes - `go build -tags kubeapiserver ./pkg/clusteragent/autoscaling/workload/metrics/...` - `go test -tags "kubeapiserver test" ./pkg/clusteragent/autoscaling/workload/metrics/...` (all pass, including the new table cases) - `go vet -tags "kubeapiserver test" ./pkg/clusteragent/autoscaling/workload/metrics/...` - `gofmt -l` reports no formatting changes needed. - Release note YAML validated as well-formed reno (`enhancements` section). New tests assert exact metric counts and per-tag/value expectations for each of the three example specs (container-resource cpu utilization 63, pod-resource cpu utilization 70, custom-query absolute value 500M), plus absolute cpu/memory unit conversions, the nil-value skip, and that two custom-query objectives produce two distinct `objective_index` series. ### Additional Notes Utilization (0–100) and absolute values (millicores/bytes/native) intentionally share one metric name, differentiated by the `value_type` tag; consumers should filter by `value_type` before graphing so units are not mixed. This is documented explicitly in `metrics.md`. The change is purely additive — no existing metric is modified, so existing dashboards and monitors are unaffected. --- PR by Bits - [View session in Datadog](https://app.datadoghq.com/code/f1899761-3730-41e5-bfad-a976d188b111) Comment @datadog to request changes

signal.title: [CWS-6628] Implement the unshare syscall event
signal.text: <!--Please give us some feedback on your experience writing this PR ! https://app.datadoghq.com/forms/43db4c02-6837-400c-8083-692e141b1b88 !--> ### What does this PR do? Adds a public `unshare` CWS event carrying the requested namespace flags, so detection rules can match the syscall itself rather than the name of the calling binary: ``` unshare.flags & CLONE_NEWNET > 0 unshare.flags & (CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET) > 0 && process.file.name != "docker" ``` New SECL surface: `unshare.flags` (bitmask, `Clone flags` constants) and `unshare.retval`. 12 `CLONE_*` constants are registered. ### Motivation Jira: [CWS-6628](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628) (also filed as [CWS-6778](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778) — duplicates). Requested by the detection guild. Recent Linux LPE exploits call `unshare` **directly** to create a new network namespace and thereby obtain `CAP_NET_ADMIN`. Today CWS can only catch this via `process.executable.name == "unshare"`, which misses every exploit that invokes the syscall from its own code. > [!NOTE] > The Jira description claims this complements an existing `setns` event. There is no `setns` instrumentation in CWS — `setns` appears only in the syscall-number tables used by the syscall-monitor event. This is CWS's first namespace-lifecycle event. Scope is unchanged; the ticket framing is just wrong. ### Describe how you validated your changes Added `pkg/security/tests/unshare_test.go` with per-flag rules plus a combined `CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWNET` case (the actual exploit shape), asserting the exact raw bitmask and `retval`. The `syscall_tester` helper invokes `unshare(2)` **directly** rather than exec'ing `unshare(1)`, since catching direct syscall callers is the point. Verified locally: | Check | Result | |---|---| | eBPF C compiles — kprobe, fentry, syscall-wrapper | all 3 objects rebuilt; `tracepoint/"handle_sys_unshare_exit"` present | | `dda inv test --targets=./pkg/security/secl/...` | 1420 passed | | `dda inv security-agent.build-functional-tests` | testsuite + `syscall_tester` build clean | | Codegen idempotent | re-ran generation, byte-identical output | | `dda inv linter.go` on secl, probe, serializers, ebpf | 0 issues | > [!IMPORTANT] > **KMT functional tests have not been run** — they need a real kernel. Since this modifies an event the mount resolver depends on, please run `TestUnshareEvent` **plus the mount, pivot_root and network suites** before merging. `syscall_tester.c:test_new_netns_exec` already calls `unshare(CLONE_NEWNET)`, so this event will start firing inside existing network tests. ### Additional Notes <details> <summary>Why the public event reuses event ordinal 46, and why that matters</summary> `unshare` was already hooked, but narrowly: the hook bailed out unless `CLONE_NEWNS` was set, and the resulting `unshare_mntns` event was swallowed in userspace after registering the mount-namespace copy (`field:"-"`, never dispatched to rules). That internal event fires **once per cloned mount** — `hook_make_visible`, `hook_attach_mnt`, `hook___attach_mnt`, `hook_attach_recursive_mnt` and `hook_propagate_mnt` each call `handle_new_mount()` for a distinct mount, which tail-calls through to `dr_mount_stage_two_callback` → `send_event`. Correct for mount bookkeeping; wrong for detection, where a rule must fire once per syscall. So the two concerns are now separate event types: - **`EVENT_UNSHARE` (ordinal 46, reusing the old slot)** — public, per-syscall. Full process/cgroup/span context plus the raw flags bitmask, sent once from the exit hook. - **`EVENT_UNSHARE_MNTNS` (newly appended)** — internal, per-mount. Semantics unchanged, still consumed by `handleNewMount` and never dispatched to rules. Keeping the *public* event at ordinal 46 is load-bearing. `probe_ebpf.go` packs enabled events as `1 << (eventType - 1)` into a **`uint64`**, mirrored kernel-side in `helpers/events.h`. `PivotRootEventType` is ordinal 64 — the last representable bit, which is exactly why `LastEventType = PivotRootEventType`. A newly appended public type would be ordinal 69 and therefore permanently unreachable by `is_event_enabled()` and by `applyDefaultFilterPolicies()`. The internal event doesn't care, since internal events are never gated by that mask. </details> <details> <summary>Event volume</summary> Bounded two independent ways: 1. **Flag allowlist** — the kernel only reports flags intersecting `CLONE_NEWUSER | CLONE_NEWNET | CLONE_NEWNS | CLONE_NEWPID`. `CLONE_NEWCGROUP` is excluded per the requester's note on CWS-6628 (it only moves the caller into the current cgroup namespace), as are the non-namespace flags. 2. **`is_event_enabled(EVENT_UNSHARE)`** — no event at all when no loaded rule references `unshare.*`. `CLONE_NEWNS` is always *cached* regardless of either gate, because the mount resolver depends on that hook entry. The `flags` field always carries the **full raw bitmask**, so rules can inspect any flag — including ones outside the allowlist — once an event fires. </details> <details> <summary>Known gap and follow-ups</summary> - In `handle_new_mount` (`mount.h`), if the mount bookkeeping bails early it calls `pop_syscall()`, dropping the cache entry before the exit hook runs — so that particular `unshare(CLONE_NEWNS)` produces no public event. Narrow degraded path, mirrors existing behaviour, but a real coverage hole for `CLONE_NEWNS` specifically. - ebpfless/ptracer support deferred, as `setrlimit` did. - `setns` instrumentation (the join-side signal) not in scope. - Four existing events (ordinals 65–68: `SampleRefresh`, `SetSid`, `Nop`, `Socket`) are already unreachable by the `enabled_events` mask and silently stay that way. Widening it past 64 bits is separate, cross-cutting work worth filing. </details> [CWS-6628]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6628?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ [CWS-6778]: https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/browse/CWS-6778?atlOrigin=eyJpIjoiNWRkNTljNzYxNjVmNDY3MDlhMDU5Y2ZhYzA5YTRkZjUiLCJwIjoiZ2l0aHViLWNvbS1KU1cifQ

signal.title: Add Observer pipeline telemetry
signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Add new and reshape existing observer telemetry. [Document](https://datadoghq.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/agent/pages/7070942507/Observer+Telemetry) Added the following: #### Ingress and admission - `observer.observations.accepted{kind,source}` counts logs and metrics successfully admitted to the Observer. - `observer.observations.dropped{kind,source}` counts observations rejected because the Observer channel is full. - `observer.logs.accepted_bytes{source}` counts admitted log-content bytes. - `observer.logs.input_rate_limiter.dropped{source,priority}` identifies logs rejected by the Observer ingress rate limiter. - `logs_adaptive_sampler.outcomes{severity,outcome}` counts eligible adaptive-sampling decisions under an applied AAD severity profile. In detection-only mode, `outcome:dropped` means the log would have been dropped. #### Retained state - `observer.log_pattern_extractor.pattern_count` is now a gauge representing all active extractor patterns, including patterns below the metric-emission threshold. - Existing `observer.series.count` and storage capacity/eviction telemetry are retained. #### Detection and output - `observer.detections.detector_emissions{detector,severity}` counts deduplicated detector output before scoring, correlation, and reporting. Severity uses `xlow|low|medium|high|xhigh`. - `observer.scorer.severity{scorer}` reports the current scorer state as `0=low`, `1=medium`, or `2=high`. - Existing `observer.scorer.ewma` and `observer.reports.emitted` are retained. #### Pipeline cost and health - `observer.log_extraction.processing_duration{extractor}` measures only each extractor's `ProcessLog` call in seconds, excluding output handling and storage. The two default-enabled extractors are `log_metrics_extractor` and `log_pattern_extractor`. - Existing in-flight, scheduler, storage, and detector-timing telemetry are retained. - The experiment will use existing Agent and Kubernetes telemetry for CPU and memory rather than introducing duplicate Observer metrics. ### Motivation We want to be able to monitor key parts of the observer pipeline. doc: [Observer Telemetry] ### Describe how you validated your changes - Unit coverage for metric types, labels, admission boundaries, extractor timing, pattern state, detector emissions, scorer severity, and adaptive-sampler outcomes. - Kind smoke test using the PR Agent image, verifying emitted metrics and labels. ### Additional Notes

signal.text: ### What does this PR do? Introduces **Windows spawn profiles** in dd-procmgr so managed children can run under different security contexts: - **Privileged**: spawn as LocalSystem (supervisor primary token) - **AgentUser**: spawn as the agent service account (`ddagentuser`) Adds the Windows spawn stack (token logon, user profile load, supervision job, suspended `CreateProcessAsUserW`), COAT catalog enforcement for allowed profiles, and gRPC pipe caller authentication. **Stack context:** PR 1/4 split from [#53249](https://github.com/DataDog/datadog-agent/pull/53249).
